extracted.intended_audience: researchers, conference organizers, and authors interested in peer review and rebuttal dynamics (particularly in machine learning/ICLR)
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical and LLM-assisted analysis of the ICLR 2024–2025 peer review and rebuttal process, extracting factors that predict score changes, taxonomies of strengths/weaknesses and rebuttal strategies, and operational guidance for authors and organizers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall rating (ICLR scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall rating for ICLR 2024 and 2025 is a discrete number in {1, 3, 5, 6, 8, 10}. (ICLR 2026 maps to {0,2,4,6,8,10}.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the primary numeric summary of reviewer assessment; many analyses (score-change, ranking displacement, class labels) use this discrete overall rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review score fields (soundness, presentation, contribution, confidence, overall rating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews provide structured numerical scores for soundness, presentation, contribution, confidence, and an overall rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses and prediction models use these separate fields as features and outcomes; changes are often concentrated in the overall rating while other fields remain unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review text sections (summary, strengths, weaknesses, questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The review format includes a summary of the paper, identified strengths and weaknesses, and questions for the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word counts in these sections are predictive (e.g., longer strengths correlate positively with higher ratings; longer weaknesses correlate negatively). Models use per-section word counts as features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths & weaknesses taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: A structured taxonomy of high-level categories and subcategories to label reviewer strengths and weaknesses: Novelty & Contribution, Motivation, Methodology & Technical Soundness, Experiments & Evaluation, Results, Data, Writing & Presentation, Broader Impact & Ethics, Related Work, Venue Fit, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this taxonomy (with specified subcategories such as 'insufficient baselines', 'missing ablations', 'unclear wording') for consistent LLM-based labeling and feature extraction; the paper reports category frequencies by rating group and uses them as predictors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal strategy taxonomy (coverage / stance / strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: A three-field taxonomy for author responses: coverage (Answered / Not Answered), stance (Agree/Disagree with subcategories like reject_validity, evasion, completion_claim, future_work, etc.), and strategy (evidence_backed_clarification vs generic_defense_vague with subcategories such as method_details, new_experiments, repetition, broad_assertion, bare_agreement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotate each reviewer point with these fields; evidence-backed strategies (method details, new analyses/experiments, citations) are more associated with score increases, while generic/vague defenses often result in score keep.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-backed clarification (rebuttal strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuttal responses that provide concrete technical clarifications, new experiments, new tables/figures, deeper analysis, or citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associated with higher probability of positive score changes; considered an effective author strategy. Subcategories: method_details, new_experiments, new_table_figures, analysis, experiments_in_paper, citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic/vague defense (rebuttal anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuttal responses that repeat claims, assert broad statements without support, evade the concern, promise vague future work, or only symbolically agree/disagree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tends to lead to no change ('keep') rather than improvements. Subcategories include repetition, broad_assertion, evasion, future_promise, bare_agreement_or_disagreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bare agreement/disagreement (limited rebuttal tactic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Author replies that only state agreement or disagreement without justification or evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often insufficient to change a reviewer’s score; less persuasive than evidence-backed clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage (Answered vs Not Answered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the author explicitly answered a specific reviewer weakness/question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Not Answered, other stance/strategy fields are left empty in annotation; coverage is a prerequisite for effective rebuttal strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stance subcategories (reject_validity, evasion, reject_request, contradict_statement, completion_claim, concede_point, Promise a change by camera-ready, future_work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Labels for the author’s positioning relative to the reviewer point (agreement or disagreement with fine-grained subtypes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different stances carry different implications: concessions or completion_claims (claiming the task is done) paired with evidence-backed clarification are more constructive; evasion or rejecting valid concerns is less effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-reviewer influence / reviewer convergence metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure reviewer influence as average pairwise disagreement |si − sj| across reviewers on a paper, and compute normalized change (after − before)/9 (9 = score range).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decreases indicate reviewer convergence (peer influence/consensus). Rebuttals reduce disagreement by ~9–10% overall, more so for high-quality papers (oral/spotlight).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal dynamics of review/rebuttal submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing patterns of reviewer and author activity across review and rebuttal windows (daily activity peaks near deadlines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observations: reviewer activity concentrates near review deadline; author/reviewer interaction peaks mid-to-late rebuttal; rebuttals submitted in the middle of the rebuttal period are most associated with score increases; very early or last-minute rebuttals are less effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer submission ordering bias (last-submitter generosity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer who submits last (displayed first) tends to give higher scores; in 4-review papers Reviewers 4,3,2,1 (in timestamp order) show increasing generosity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awareness of ordering/timestamp effects matters in interpreting displayed review lists; ordering is not random and correlates with score distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer engagement measures (participation %, conversation turns, number of notes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantities capturing reviewer-author interaction: author/reviewer participation percentage, conversation turns (ConvTurn), and reviewer note counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher engagement (more conversation turns, higher participation) correlates with increased likelihood of score increases; however, active discussions can also correlate with score decreases — engagement is necessary but not sufficient and outcome depends on content/stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ranking displacement as rebuttal impact metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the percentage of papers displaced from top-x ranked positions before vs after rebuttal-induced score changes (a proxy for acceptance impact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess whether rebuttals change relative ordering; results show substantial displacement among top-ranked papers (e.g., >40% of top 5% displaced), indicating small score shifts can matter greatly when acceptance is competitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score-change distribution / typical transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Observed frequent score updates concentrate in mid-range (5→6, 6→8, 3→5) and most review scores remain unchanged (2024: 81%, 2025: 75%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rebuttal impact is concentrated on borderline papers; authors should focus effort where small changes can change outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count features as predictive signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Word counts of review sections (strengths, weaknesses, summary, questions) correlate with scores: overall rating positively correlates with strengths-word-count and negatively with weaknesses-word-count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In modeling reviewer decisions, include per-section word counts; reviewers with higher confidence write longer weaknesses and tend to give lower overall ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top predictive features for rating classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Important features for predicting pre-rebuttal overall rating include: Novelty & Contribution (weakness/strength), Experiments & Evaluation, Word Count, Writing & Presentation, Methodology & Technical Soundness, Motivation, Results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretability-focused models (e.g., multinomial logistic regression) allow ranking feature importances; use combined textual category labels and word counts for better performance than word counts alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection requirement for tracking score changes
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReview displays only final versions and overwrites preliminary reviews; therefore, to measure score changes, data must be archived both immediately after initial reviews and again after rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational requirement for reproducible analysis: capture snapshots at both times; failing to do so will miss before-rebuttal scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal outcome predictors (initial score and co-reviewers' scores)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial overall rating and the mean of other reviewers' scores are among the strongest predictors of whether a reviewer will change their score after rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are hard-to-change, pre-existing factors; authors can influence outcomes primarily via targeted, evidence-backed rebuttals, but baseline scores and peer reviewer influence dominate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal strategy feature coefficients (what shifts decisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model coefficients indicate which strategies/features are associated with DEC (decrease), INC (increase), or KEEP: e.g., high initial rating predicts decrease; mean other reviewers' rating predicts increase or decrease depending on direction; generic/vague defense contributes to KEEP; evidence-backed clarification contributes to INC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use coefficients to prioritize rebuttal content: emphasize evidence-backed clarifications and method details when attempting to increase scores; avoid generic defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-dependent rebuttal / convergence effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Rebuttal-induced reviewer convergence varies by submission category: largest reductions in disagreement for spotlight/oral, moderate for posters, and minimal for rejected/withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect stronger co-reviewer influence on higher-quality submissions; rebuttal utility varies by submission outcome stratum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most changes are in overall rating (scope limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most reviews (71% of cases) reflect changes only in the overall score and do not update other aspects (e.g., soundness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When modeling rebuttal effects focus primarily on overall rating changes but be aware other fields rarely change; targeted rebuttals addressing specific fields are less often used to update those fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical author guidance derived from analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirically grounded suggestions: focus rebuttal effort on borderline/mid-range papers (where small changes matter), submit rebuttals in mid-rebuttal window, prioritize evidence-backed clarifications addressing reviewers' concrete concerns, and engage where reviewers show willingness to interact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid last-minute or rushed rebuttals; do not rely on vague promises or bare agreement; explicitly address reviewer points with concrete data, method details, or new analyses if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotation protocol constraints for human/LLM labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Weakness/strength annotation prompts require mapping each paragraph to predefined categories/subcategories (avoid using 'Other' unless impossible), extracting exact text spans, and annotating multiple items per paragraph where present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict annotation rules improve label consistency (the paper reports ~81–84% pairwise human agreement with chosen prompts); replicate these constraints when building datasets for supervised models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal immediate-effect observation (rapid early updates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many reviewer score changes (mostly increases) occur within the first hour after review release (i.e., influence can take effect immediately).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that some score adjustments happen quickly after reviews are public—models of influence should consider very short timescales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance is not guaranteed by score increase (limit of rebuttal)
rubrics_metrics.description: A substantial fraction of papers with increased reviewer scores were still not accepted (42% in 2024, 44% in 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score improvements help but do not ensure acceptance; meta-reviews and chair-level decisions depend on additional factors (topic interest, overall review quality, ranking).
